result: TIME cells were validated as a suitable model for studying hantavirus entry in endothelial cells. The cells express endothelial markers (PECAM-1, vWF) and candidate receptors (PCDH1, β3 integrin, β1 integrin, DAF) similarly to primary HUVECs, and support entry by divergent hantavirus glycoproteins.
evaluation: Claims C33-C37 establish TIME cells as an appropriate model through expression profiling (Figure 1a) and functional susceptibility assays (Figure 2). The characterization includes proper controls (HUVEC comparison) and multiple validation methods (flow cytometry, infection assays). The conclusion (C37) logically follows from the data.

result: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout cell lines were successfully generated and validated for PCDH1, ITGB3, DAF, and ITGB1. Knockout was confirmed at genomic (Sanger sequencing showing frameshifts), protein surface (flow cytometry), and total protein (western blot) levels.
evaluation: Claims C63-C68 describe rigorous validation of knockout cell lines using multiple orthogonal methods. Figure 1—figure supplement 1 shows all sequenced clones contained frameshifting indels, and Figures 1b,c confirm loss of protein expression. The methodology is sound with appropriate controls (WT cells, complementation).

result: PCDH1 knockout substantially reduced entry by New-World hantaviruses (ANDV, SNV, CHOV, MPRLV, PHV) but not Old-World hantaviruses (HTNV, PUUV, SEOV, DOBV) in rVSV pseudotype assays. This effect was rescued by PCDH1 cDNA complementation. In contrast, knockout of ITGB3 or DAF had no effect on entry by any tested hantavirus.
evaluation: Claims C38-C44 present the core pseudovirus findings with appropriate statistical analysis (two-way ANOVA, p<0.0001 for PCDH1 effects; Figure 2b-d). The complementation rescue (C43) provides critical specificity control. The lack of ITGB3/DAF effects is consistently observed across multiple viruses with adequate replication (n=11-12). Data strongly support differential PCDH1 dependence between New-World and Old-World hantaviruses.

result: Double knockout experiments ruled out functional redundancy between candidate receptors. PCDH1/ITGB3 and PCDH1/DAF double knockouts phenocopied PCDH1 single knockouts, while ITGB3/DAF double knockouts remained fully susceptible to ANDV and SNV entry (only ~25% reduction for HTNV).
evaluation: Claims C45-C49 address the important alternative hypothesis of receptor redundancy through double knockout analysis (Figure 2d). The data convincingly demonstrate that ITGB3 and DAF loss does not unmask requirements when PCDH1 is absent, and vice versa. Statistical analysis confirms significance (p<0.0001). This strengthens the conclusion that ITGB3/DAF are dispensable.

result: Authentic hantavirus infections confirmed pseudovirus results: PCDH1 knockout reduced infection by New-World viruses (ANDV, SNV, PHV) with no effect from ITGB3, DAF, or ITGB1 knockout. qPCR showed 95% reduction in SNV genome replication in PCDH1-deficient cells (5±2%) versus no reduction in ITGB3 (108±15%) or DAF (82±13%) knockouts.
evaluation: Claims C50-C54, C56 validate key findings using authentic viruses rather than pseudotypes (Figure 2e), addressing a potential limitation. The qPCR data (C52-C54) provide quantitative confirmation with appropriate replication (n=6 from two experiments). Statistical significance is demonstrated (p<0.0001). The consistency between pseudovirus and authentic virus results strengthens conclusions substantially.

result: Among candidate receptors tested (β3 integrin, β1 integrin, DAF, PCDH1), only PCDH1 genetic loss reduced hantavirus infection in endothelial cells. The authors conclude that β3 integrin, β1 integrin, and DAF are dispensable for viral entry in endothelial cells.
evaluation: Claims C5-C6, C58-C59 summarize the main findings. The conclusion (C59) is well-supported by convergent evidence from multiple experimental approaches (pseudovirus, authentic virus, single/double knockouts, complementation) across a large panel of hantaviruses. The data directly challenge long-standing assumptions in the field (C3, C22) with rigorous genetic evidence that was previously lacking (C4, C31).

result: The authors conclude that major host molecules necessary for endothelial cell entry by PCDH1-independent Old-World hantaviruses (HTNV, PUUV, SEOV, DOBV) remain to be discovered, as none of the tested candidate receptors were required.
evaluation: Claims C7, C32, C42 present an important inference from negative results. Since Old-World hantaviruses do not require PCDH1 (C39, C42) and the other candidates are dispensable (C40, C44, C51), unknown receptors must exist. This conclusion is logically sound given the data, though it identifies a knowledge gap rather than filling it. The claim is appropriately cautious.

result: The authors note their results do not rule out roles for β3 integrin, β1 integrin, or DAF in: (1) hantavirus entry into other cell types, (2) entry into polarized cells, or (3) post-entry endothelial cell subversion.
evaluation: Claims C60-C62 appropriately acknowledge limitations and alternative interpretations. The study specifically examined non-polarized endothelial cells, so these caveats are scientifically valid. This demonstrates appropriate scientific caution and prevents overgeneralization of findings. The speculation is reasonable and grounded in prior literature (citations provided).

result: Prior work established β3/β1-containing integrins and DAF as presumed hantavirus receptors based on complementation and blocking studies, but rigorous genetic loss-of-function evidence was lacking. These candidates were not identified in unbiased genetic screens.
evaluation: Claims C3-C4, C20-C22, C30-C31 accurately characterize prior literature and identify the knowledge gap this study addresses. The characterization is supported by appropriate citations and represents the historical context fairly. The distinction between prior evidence types (complementation/blocking) and genetic knockout approaches is scientifically important.

result: Prior work by the authors identified PCDH1 as a critical receptor for New-World but not Old-World hantaviruses in primary endothelial cells, with genetic depletion reducing entry/infection in vitro and protecting hamsters from lethal disease in vivo.
evaluation: Claims C23-C29 accurately summarize prior published work (Jangra et al., 2018) that established PCDH1's role. These claims provide essential context for the current study, which extends those findings by systematically testing other candidate receptors. The citations are appropriate and the characterization appears accurate.

result: Background claims establish that hantaviruses are RNA viruses causing severe zoonotic diseases (HFRS, HCPS) with epidemic potential, no approved therapeutics, and endothelial cells as primary infection targets in humans.
evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C8-C19, C57 provide standard background information supported by appropriate citations and established knowledge. These contextual claims are accurate and well-documented in the literature. They establish the medical importance and rationale for the study.

result: Prior hypotheses suggested β1 integrin as a receptor for avirulent hantaviruses.
evaluation: Claim C55 accurately cites prior literature (Gavrilovskaya et al., 1998) proposing β1 integrin's role. This provides context for testing ITGB1 knockout effects on PHV (an avirulent virus), which showed no requirement (C56).
